findings.title: canManage() grants manage to holders of only the view scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the 'view' scope on all Groups passes canManage(). requireManage() is based on this method and is used e.g. by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup to create top-level groups, so a view-only FGAP admin can create groups (and perform other operations gated only by requireManage()). canManage() should require only the MANAGE scope, as canManage(GroupModel) on line 79 already does.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs/names
findings.body: Resources for Groups are looked up by name, where the resource name is the group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and hasPermission(String) does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)). Here the code passes groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource's own UUID) to hasPermission, so findByName misses and evaluation falls back to the all-Groups resource, ignoring per-group view-members/manage-members grants. It then adds groupResource.getId() to the result, but callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource expect actual group IDs for the UserModel.GROUPS filter. Consequently admins with per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS see no group members in user searches/counts. Both places should use groupResource.getName().

findings.title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users resource type, returning the username for a user resource and 'All users' for the type resource. For the newly added Groups type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), but group resources created by getOrCreateResource have the group ID as their name and no display name set, so permission listings for group resources will show a null/blank or raw ID instead of the group name (and no 'All groups' label). Add the analogous Groups branch resolving the group by resource name and returning its name.
